args.sql:
SELECT 
    p.patkey AS patient_id,
    ab.abkey AS assessment_id,
    e.timemark AS latest_assessment_date,
    ROUND(AVG(aasr.mental_health_scores->'symptom_scores'::text[1]::decimal)) AS avg_rounded_tes_score,
    f.envstress AS site_stress_indicator
FROM 
    patients p
JOIN 
    assessmentbasics ab ON p.patkey = ab.patownerref
JOIN 
    encounters e ON ab.abkey = e.abref
JOIN 
    facilities f ON e.facid = f.fackey
JOIN 
    treatmentbasics tb ON e.enckey = tb.encref
JOIN 
    assessmentsymptomsandrisk aasr ON ab.abkey = aasr.asrkey
WHERE 
    f.envstress = 'Severe'
    AND tb.therapy_details->>'engagement' = 'Low'
GROUP BY 
    p.patkey, ab.abkey, e.timemark, f.envstress
ORDER BY 
    e.timemark DESC
LIMIT 10;

Database: mental
Task ID: mental_1

User Query:
I want to identify urgent-risk Patients from facilities experiencing high stress, who also have weak engagement in therapy. For each patient, include their patient ID, assessment ID, date of their most recent assessment, their average rounded TES score, and the site's stress indicator they are associated with. Focus only on the most recent assessments and prioritize patients meeting all these criteria. Sort the results and just return the top results.

You have a budget of 22.0 bird-coins. Use your tools to explore the database, clarify ambiguities with the user, and submit your final SQL efficiently.
